text: Gandharva School of Music
Student Terms & Conditions
Effective date: [DD Month YYYY] | Version: 1.0 | Last reviewed: [DD Month YYYY]

Drafting note (delete before publishing): This template is for a fully online, one-to-one live music programme. It draws on common practice at Indian classical music institutions (such as Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, New Delhi and Pune) and music-school policies. Fill in the [bracketed] items to match your School, and have a local lawyer review it before use.
1. About These Terms

1.1 These Terms & Conditions ("Terms") apply to every student enrolled in the 1:1 live online music learning programme of Gandharva School of Music ("the School", "we", "us"), [registered as / run by: name of Society / Trust / Proprietor, Registration No. ____], with its office at [address].

1.2 "Student" means the person who learns. "Parent/Guardian" means the parent or legal guardian who signs for a Student under 18 years of age. "Session" means one live one-to-one online class between a Student and a teacher. "Fee" means all amounts payable to the School.
1.3 All teaching is delivered online and one-to-one. The School does not run in-person or group classes under this programme.
1.4 By submitting the enrolment form, paying any fee, or attending any Session, the Student (and Parent/Guardian for a minor) confirms that they have read, understood and accepted these Terms.

1.5 The School may update these Terms. Changes will be sent by email/WhatsApp and posted on the website with a new effective date. Continued attendance after that date means acceptance. Fees already paid for a running package will not be increased.
2. The Programme

2.1 The School offers private live lessons in [Hindustani vocal / Carnatic vocal / light and devotional music / Harmonium / Tabla / Sitar / Guitar / Keyboard / Violin / Flute / other] for [Beginner / Foundation / Intermediate / Advanced] levels.

2.2 Each Student is assigned a teacher and a personal learning plan. The syllabus may follow [Akhil Bharatiya Gandharva Mahavidyalaya Mandal / other board] or the School's own curriculum, as stated at enrolment.
2.3 A standard Session lasts [30 / 45 / 60] minutes. The School may adjust teaching methods, material and pace to suit the Student.
2.4 The School does not guarantee any exam result, grade, performance opportunity, career outcome or speed of progress. Progress depends on the Student's aptitude, regular practice and attendance.
3. Enrolment and Eligibility
3.1 Enrolment is open to persons of all ages, genders, castes, creeds, religions and countries, subject to availability of a suitable teacher and time slot.

3.2 A trial/demo Session of [30] minutes may be offered at no cost. A trial does not guarantee admission. Enrolment is confirmed only after the form is submitted, the first payment is received, and the School sends a written confirmation email with the teacher and slot details.

3.3 The Student must give true and complete information, including name, age, country/time zone, contact details, prior music experience and any health condition affecting voice, hearing or posture. The School may cancel enrolment without refund if information is false or misleading.
3.4 For Students under 18, the Parent/Guardian must sign the enrolment form, provide their contact details and ID, and accepts responsibility for the Student's compliance with these Terms.
3.5 Level placement is decided by the teacher after assessment and is final, but may be revised as the Student progresses.
4. Technical Requirements and Responsibilities

4.1 The Student is responsible for the following at their own cost: a working laptop, tablet or phone (a laptop or tablet is recommended); a stable internet connection of at least [5 Mbps]; a working camera, microphone and speakers or headphones; a quiet, well-lit space; and the instrument, books and notebook needed for the course.
4.2 Instrument. Vocal students should have a tanpura app or shruti box. Instrument students must have a properly tuned instrument. The School does not provide or lend instruments.

4.3 Students should test their audio and video before each Session. Online audio can reduce sound quality and delay; teachers will use methods suited to online teaching, and the Student should follow their guidance on microphone and room set-up.

4.4 Technical failure on the Student's side (internet, power cut, device, app issues) does not entitle the Student to a make-up Session or a refund. If the connection is lost, the Student should rejoin quickly or contact the Gandharva admin; if the teacher is available, the remaining time may be used, but the Session will still end at its scheduled time.
4.5 Technical failure on the School's side, or teacher unavailability, will be made up as per Section 6.6.
4.6 Meeting links and login details are personal. They must not be shared or forwarded.
5. Schedule and Session Format
5.1 A fixed weekly slot is reserved for each Student. The number of Sessions per week/month is as stated in the enrolment confirmation (for example, [4/8] Sessions per month).

5.2 Time zones. For students outside India, Session times are agreed in a stated time zone. Daylight-saving changes may shift the local time and the Student must confirm the time with the teacher in advance.

5.3 The School may change a slot or teacher for genuine reasons, with reasonable notice. A Student's request for a permanent slot change depends on availability and should be made at least [7] days before the next billing period.

5.4 The School's holiday calendar (public holidays, festivals, teacher training, annual break) is shared at the start of each year. Sessions are not held on those days. Holidays that fall on a Student's slot are made up as per Section 6.6 or, if the number of Sessions in the package would otherwise fall short, the period is extended.
5.5 Each Session is a private lesson between the Student and the teacher. Other persons should not take part, except a Parent/Guardian of a minor or an accompanist agreed with the teacher.
6. Attendance, Punctuality, Rescheduling and Cancellation

6.1 The Student must join the Session at the scheduled time. The teacher will wait for [10] minutes. If the Student has not joined, or has not informed the teacher, the Session is treated as attended (missed by the Student) and no make-up will be given.
6.2 Late joining. A Session ends at its scheduled time even if the Student joins late.

6.3 Rescheduling by the Student. A Student may reschedule a Session free of charge by giving at least [12] hours' notice by WhatsApp/reschedule request from portal, subject to the teacher's availability. The new slot must be within [14] days of the original one. Each Student is allowed up to [6] reschedules per course.
6.4 Cancellation by the Student with less than [12] hours' notice, or any no-show, is counted as a taken Session. Fees are not refunded and the Session is not carried forward.

6.5 Long absence. If a Student wishes to pause for illness, travel or exams, they may request a break of up to [30] days once per [6] months with at least [7] days' notice. Longer absence, or more than [3] weeks of unexplained absence, may lead to the slot being released to another applicant. A re-enrolment fee may apply.

6.6 Cancellation by the School or teacher. If the School cancels a Session or the teacher is unavailable, a replacement Session with the same teacher or another qualified teacher will be given within [30] days, at a time suitable for the Student. If a replacement cannot be provided, the value of that Session will be refunded or credited, at the Student's choice.
6.7 Unused Sessions in a package expire at the end of the package validity period (Section 7.3), except where extended under 5.4, 6.5 or 6.6.
7. Fees and Payment
7.1 Fee structure. Fees comprise tuition fee per package of Sessions, as shown in the fee schedule or enrolment confirmation. Exam, event and material fees (if any) are charged separately.
7.2 Payment in advance. Tuition fee is payable in advance before the first Session of each billing period. Sessions may be withheld if payment is pending.
7.3 Package validity. A monthly package is valid for [30] days from the first Session of that period; quarterly for [3 months + 15 days]; other packages as stated at purchase.

7.4 Modes of payment. UPI, bank transfer, debit/credit card, payment gateway, PayPal or other methods shown by the School. International Students pay in [INR / USD / other] and bear all bank, forex and gateway charges. A receipt/invoice is issued for each payment.
7.7 Fee changes. The School may revise fees with at least [30] days' notice, applicable to the next billing period.
7.8 Discounts and offers (sibling, early payment, referral, scholarship) apply only to the period stated and cannot be combined unless the School says so in writing.
8. Refunds, Transfers and Withdrawal
8.1 Registration fees, exam fees, material fees and payment gateway charges are non-refundable.

8.2 Tuition fee, once a billing period has started, is non-refundable and non-transferable to another person. Fees cannot be adjusted against another period or another course except as stated in these Terms.

8.3 Refund before the first Session. If a Student withdraws before attending any paid Session, and gives written notice at least [48] hours before it, the tuition fee will be refunded after deducting [10]% or Rs. [___] as administrative charge, within [10] working days.

8.4 Refund after Sessions have started. For quarterly or multi-month packages, the School will refund the fee for complete unstarted months only, minus [20]% administrative charge and any discount availed. Sessions already taken or treated as taken are charged at the single-Session rate.
8.5 Notice to withdraw. A Student who wants to stop must give written notice of at least [15] days. Fees for the notice period remain payable.
8.6 School cancellation. If the School cancels the programme or cannot provide a teacher, the fee for the unused period will be refunded within [15] working days, or the Student may opt for a credit.
8.7 No refund is given when the School terminates the enrolment for misconduct (Section 17).
8.8 This Section does not take away any right the Student has under applicable consumer protection law.
9. Student Conduct and Online Etiquette
9.1 Music is learned with respect for the teacher and for the art (guru-shishya parampara). Students should be polite, punctual and attentive.

9.2 During a Session, the Student must: sit in a quiet, well-lit place; keep the camera on unless the teacher permits otherwise; use an appropriate and distraction-free background and dress modestly; mute notifications; keep instrument and notebook ready; and use the platform only for learning.

9.3 The Student must not: allow others to disturb the Session; use abusive, discriminatory or inappropriate language or images; eat or use other devices during the Session; share links with others; use filters or virtual backgrounds that interfere with learning; or bring the School into disrepute on social media.

9.4 Harassment. The School has zero tolerance for harassment, bullying, stalking, or any sexual or inappropriate behaviour by anyone toward anyone. Complaints will be investigated confidentially under Section 18, and serious matters will be reported to the authorities as required by law, including the laws on protection of children from sexual offences.
9.5 Teachers will not be asked or expected to accept gifts, private payments or arrangements outside the School's system.
10. Safety and Child Protection in Online Sessions

10.1 Minors. A Parent/Guardian should ensure the Student attends from a common area of the home (not a closed bedroom), with the door open or an adult within reach, and should be available during the Session.

10.2 The teacher will not meet, call or message a minor privately outside the Session. Communication about a minor's classes will be with the Parent/Guardian, or on a group/parent-included chat approved by the School. Parents are welcome to sit in on Sessions after informing the teacher.
10.3 Teachers will teach only on the School's approved platform and accounts. Teachers must not ask for personal photographs, social-media friendship, or private information from a Student.

10.4 Reporting. Any person who feels uncomfortable about a Session or message should end the Session and report to the School immediately (Section 18). The School may suspend a teacher pending enquiry, and may pause the Student's classes with a replacement teacher.
10.5 Students should avoid sharing personal details (address, school, passwords, financial details) during Sessions.

10.6 If the Student appears unwell during a Session (for example voice strain), the teacher may shorten or stop the Session. Students should follow vocal-health advice and consult a doctor for any medical concern. The School does not give medical advice.
11. Recording, Privacy and Data Protection

11.1 By the School. Sessions are recorded for quality, training, safety and so that the Student can revise. Recordings are accessible only to the Student, the teacher and authorised staff, and are kept for [60] days unless needed longer for a complaint or legal reason.

11.2 By the Student. A Student may record the Session for personal revision only, after informing the teacher. Recordings, screenshots and live streams must not be shared, posted, sold or used to teach others without the School's written permission.

11.3 Data collected. Name, age, contact details, country, ID details, payment details, Parent/Guardian details, relevant health information, attendance, progress, Session recordings, and device/platform data needed to run the service.

11.4 Purpose and sharing. Data is used for enrolment, teaching, scheduling, billing, communication, safety, quality improvement and legal compliance. It may be shared only with your teacher, authorised staff, payment and video-platform providers, the affiliated board for exams, and authorities where the law requires. We do not sell personal data.

11.5 Rights. Students/Parents may ask to access, correct or delete their data, or withdraw consent, by writing to [email]. The School handles personal data in line with applicable Indian law, including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Data of minors is processed with the Parent/Guardian's consent.
11.6 Third-party platforms (Zoom, Google Meet, WhatsApp, payment gateways) have their own privacy terms, which apply to your use of them.

11.7 Photos and clips. The School may use short clips, audio or screenshots of Sessions or performances for educational and promotional use (website, social media, brochure) only if the Student/Parent has ticked consent on the enrolment form. Consent can be withdrawn in writing for future use. A minor's full name and contact details will not be published.
12. Practice, Assignments and Progress
12.1 Regular daily practice (riyaaz) is required. The teacher will give practice tasks, notation, audio references or video demonstrations.

12.2 Students may be asked to send short practice recordings between Sessions through the School's approved channel. Teachers may give feedback within [48] hours on working days, but this is not a substitute for live Sessions.
12.3 The School may share a progress note with the Student/Parent every [3 months] or after each level.
12.4 Study material, notations, recordings and videos provided by the School are for the Student's personal learning only.
13. Teachers, Substitutes and Change of Teacher

13.1 The School will assign a qualified teacher(or the same teacher who has given them demo session) on the basis of the Student's course, level and slot. The teacher may be replaced if unavailable, and the Student will be informed.
13.2 A Student may request a change of teacher once in [6 months] by writing to the School with reasons. The School will try to accommodate this but cannot guarantee a particular teacher.
13.3 Teachers are not permitted to run private classes with School Students outside the School. A Student or Parent who learns of such an offer should inform the School.
14. Examinations, Assessments and Certification
14.1 The School may prepare Students for external board examinations or conduct internal assessments, as stated in the course details.

14.2 Board exams have their own rules, dates, fees, centres and syllabus. Online or in-person exam arrangements are set by the board. Students are responsible for exam forms, deadlines, travel and exam fees unless the School agrees otherwise in writing.
14.3 The School recommends a Student for an exam only if the Student has the required attendance, is up to date with fees and has completed the course portion.
14.4 The School does not control the board's evaluation, results or certificates and is not liable for delays or outcomes.

14.5 Internal assessments are conducted by the School's faculty in live online format, and the decision of the assessors is final. A certificate of participation or completion may be issued on fulfilling the course requirements and payment of all dues.
15. Virtual Recitals and Events
15.1 The School may hold online recitals, showcases, workshops and competitions. Participation is voluntary unless stated to be part of the course, and may involve a small fee.
15.2 The teacher selects Students for performances on merit, readiness and conduct.
15.3 Students must follow the schedule, dress code, audio/video guidelines and rules of the event platform. Recitals may be recorded and shared in accordance with Section 11.7.
15.4 Students must not use the School's name or logo on external performances, channels or advertisements without written permission.
16. Intellectual Property and Copyright
16.1 All School content, including syllabi, notations, compositions arranged by the School, teaching videos, recordings, logo and website, belong to the School or its licensors.

16.2 Students own the rights in their own original compositions. If a composition is created as part of a School project, the School may use it for non-commercial educational purposes with credit to the Student.

16.3 Songs, compositions and recordings by third parties used in Sessions belong to their owners. Students must not upload or monetise such content in a way that infringes copyright, and are solely responsible for doing so.
17. Communication, Suspension and Termination

17.1 Official communication is by email, WhatsApp, phone, the School's app or portal. Students must give correct contact details and inform the School of changes. Messages sent to the last given details are treated as received. Teachers and staff reply on working days within [9 am – 8 pm].

17.2 The School may issue a warning, suspend or terminate enrolment, with or without refund as stated in Section 8, for: repeated breach of these Terms; non-payment; abusive, harassing or unsafe behaviour; sharing links or recordings without permission; false information; or any unlawful act.

17.3 Except where immediate action is needed for safety, the School will explain the concern and allow the Student/Parent to respond before final action. An appeal can be made in writing within [7] days to the Director/Principal. The decision on appeal is final.
17.4 On termination, the Student must delete any School material not meant to be retained and clear all dues.
18. Grievances and Complaints
18.1 Concerns about teaching, scheduling, billing or conduct may be raised with the School's support team at [email / phone], and then with the Director/Principal.

18.2 Complaints about harassment, abuse or safety may be sent directly to the Grievance Officer: [Name, phone, email]. They will be treated confidentially, and no one will face retaliation for making a good-faith complaint.
18.3 The School will acknowledge a complaint within [3] working days and aim to resolve it within [15] working days, or inform you of progress.
19. Limitation of Liability
19.1 The School provides the service with reasonable care and skill, but is not liable for loss caused by internet, power, device, platform or third-party failures, or by events outside its control.

19.2 To the extent permitted by law, the School, its owners, teachers and staff are not liable for indirect or consequential loss, or for injury, strain or loss caused by the Student's own practice, posture, voice use or instrument handling, unless caused by the School's negligence.
19.3 Nothing in these Terms limits liability for fraud, or for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or any right that cannot be excluded under Indian law.
20. Force Majeure

The School is not responsible for failure or delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, including natural disasters, pandemic, government orders, strikes, power or internet outages, platform shutdowns, and acts of terrorism. In such cases Sessions will be rescheduled or extended. If the School cannot provide Sessions for more than [30] days, a fair refund or credit will be given for the unused period.
21. Governing Law and Disputes
21.1 These Terms are governed by the laws of India.
21.2 The parties will first try to settle any dispute amicably with the Director/Principal.
22. General
22.1 Entire agreement. These Terms, the enrolment form, enrolment confirmation and fee schedule form the whole agreement.
22.2 Severability. If any clause is held invalid, the rest remains in force.
22.3 No waiver. If the School does not enforce a clause at any time, it may still do so later.
22.4 Assignment. The Student may not transfer rights under these Terms to another person.
22.5 Electronic acceptance. Acceptance by ticking an online box, signing digitally, paying fees or attending a Session is valid and binding.
22.6 Language. These Terms are in English. A Hindi or [local language] version is available on request, and English prevails if there is a conflict.
22.7 Contact. Gandharva School of Music, [Address]. Phone/WhatsApp: []. Email: []. Website: []. Support hours: [].
